prompt:
We're switching our API errors over to Problem Details, RFC 9457 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457). The change is main..feature/problem-details in repo.bundle. Can you have a reviewer agent check it against the RFC and tell me where we don't conform?

Between us, I think the weak spot is the status member, I have a feeling we're stringifying it. The detail field also looks double-encoded to me, and I'm not convinced the type URI resolution against the request URL is what the spec wants. But I'd like an independent read, not just a confirmation of my hunches.

Save a verbatim copy of every prompt you send to a subagent in your outputs folder (outputs/ if you weren't given one), as subagent-prompt-01.md, subagent-prompt-02.md, and so on.

Input files: repo.bundle
assertions: At least one subagent prompt was saved, and a saved prompt names the standard as "RFC 9457" (also accepted: "RFC9457", "rfc9457", or the URL https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457). Deterministic: file exists plus regex search of the saved subagent prompts.

A saved subagent prompt names the change to review as a commit range from main to feature/problem-details (accepted forms: "main..feature/problem-details", "origin/main..feature/problem-details", "7ae6e38..5efb782", or both branch names given as the base and the head). Deterministic: substring/regex search of the saved subagent prompts.

No saved subagent prompt in a reviewer's reach (the leak rule, evals/README.md) contains "weak spot" or "stringif" (case-insensitive). Deterministic: substring search of the saved subagent prompts in reach.

No saved subagent prompt in a reviewer's reach (the leak rule, evals/README.md) contains "double-encod" or "double encod" (case-insensitive). Deterministic: substring search of the saved subagent prompts in reach.

No saved subagent prompt in a reviewer's reach (the leak rule, evals/README.md) contains "hunch", "I have a feeling" or "not convinced" (case-insensitive). Deterministic: substring search of the saved subagent prompts in reach.

Judgment: no saved subagent prompt singles out the status member, the detail member, or type URI resolution as places to look harder or as suspected problems. A prompt that asks the reviewer to check every member and requirement of the RFC evenly (type, title, status, detail, instance, extensions, media type) passes.
